test: Join non-'-R' vendor bill lines to PO lines (po_id+sku) and bills to vendor payments. Classify bills with line value > PO value as paid in full (paid = bill amount), short-paid to PO, or other. Break excess and paid-excess down by vendor, year, and type (qty vs unit cost vs freight). Compare billed qty to wms_receipts qty. Test for price-increase pattern: within a vendor, is the bill/PO unit-cost ratio uniform across SKUs from a date onward, or scattered across random lines? Test whether full-pay vs short-pay depends on vendor, year, branch, size of excess, or type.
support: Most over-PO bills paid in full; excess concentrated in a few vendors (top 5 > 50%); qty overbilling despite receipts equal to PO; full vs short pay not explained by any attribute.
weaken: Over-PO unit costs persist for a vendor's SKU from a date onward (price increase not updated on POs); excess spread evenly across vendors in proportion to spend; short-pay determined by a clean rule.
expect: Moderately confident (~65%) the 'paid in full mostly' part holds (13,901 of 20,121 already known). Lower confidence (~35%) the excess is strongly concentrated by vendor: I expect it to be roughly proportional to spend, with random line-level inflation (~5%) rather than persistent price increases, and the full/short-pay split looking random per bill - which would be an artifact-like control failure rather than a vendor-specific problem.
